function.mechanism: Bisulfite/sulfite species act as reducing agents and antimicrobial stressors, helping suppress oxidation/browning and microbial growth in preserved foods.
common_food_categories: processed foods and beverages using sulfite preservation
products requiring sulfite declaration at detectable levels (>=10 ppm)

adi.basis: Temporary group ADI of 0.7 mg/kg bw/day (as SO2 equivalents) was set in 2016 and withdrawn in 2022 follow-up due unresolved toxicological uncertainty.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA follow-up withdrew the temporary group ADI and indicated potential concern for high consumers in later refined exposure work.

adi.basis: Group ADI (0-0.7) expressed as sulfur dioxide for sulfites including sodium hydrogen sulfite.

concerns.summary: Experimental study (2022) reported sodium bisulfite-associated biothiol imbalance, ROS/NF-kB activation, and intestinal inflammatory effects in cell/mouse models.
In vitro work found sulfites (including sodium bisulfite) inhibited several beneficial gut bacterial species at tested concentrations relevant to food preservative contexts.
Recent dermatology literature reports sulfite-related sensitization/contact-allergy signals (primarily metabisulfite data), indicating class-level hypersensitivity concern in susceptible individuals.

no_concern_confirmed: IARC list dataset classifies related entries "Sulfites" and "Sulfur dioxide" as Group 3 (not classifiable as to carcinogenicity to humans).
FDA lists sodium bisulfite as GRAS under specified GMP restrictions (21 CFR 182.3739).

populations: high consumers across multiple age groups
adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA 2016 reported temporary ADI exceedance in younger groups; EFSA 2025 refined assessment reported concern for high consumers via MOE/BMDL approach after ADI withdrawal.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory approval remains, but EFSA's temporary ADI was withdrawn and high-consumer concern persists in refined exposure assessment; mechanistic and hypersensitivity signals support caution without meeting high-tier criteria such as major bans or stronger carcinogenic classification.
key_factors: EFSA high-consumer concern in refined exposure work (2025)
FDA GRAS status with explicit restrictions (21 CFR 182.3739)
IARC related sulfite entries are Group 3
